description.value: A voxel-based morphometry study of grey matter volume associations with recognition of musical, facial and vocal emotions in patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration.

spans.text: Here we investigated the neuroanatomical substrate for recognition of musical emotion in a cohort of 26 patients with FTLD

value: we hypothesised that emotion recognition from music in FTLD would be vulnerable to the effects of damage involving distributed brain circuitry for representing and evaluating the emotional content of stimuli.

we hypothesised that recognition of emotion in music would place particular demands on brain mechanisms involved in analysis and evaluation of the emotional content of complex social signals, including OFC, medial prefrontal and anterior temporal cortex.

description.value: Participants matched each target stimulus with the most appropriate verbal emotion label in a four-alternative-forced-choice paradigm.

instructions.value: Match each target stimulus with the most appropriate verbal emotion label.

stimuli.value: Ten examples of each of four target emotions were presented in each modality, for 40 trials per modality. Music stimuli were approximately 11-second non-vocal orchestral and chamber excerpts from Western classical music and film scores.

value: Total emotion recognition score out of 40
